//: Which classes of action an agent may take on its own, and which stop and wait for the owner. This is a TABLE read by code, not advice in a prompt: an approval is required by the task state machine itself (transitions.mjs), so there is no path to `in_progress` that skips it, and the MCP surface contains no tool that can grant one.
//evaluation: ALL rules are evaluated and the HIGHEST severity among the matches wins; approval is mandatory if any match says so. First-match-wins was rejected: it makes rule ORDER load-bearing, so reordering the file can silently downgrade a rule. An action that matches nothing falls to `unmatched_class` — SECURITY_SENSITIVE, i.e. ask — because a classifier that fails open is not a classifier.

READ_ONLY.summary: Reads the tree, git, docs or test output. Changes nothing.

SAFE_WRITE.summary: Edits source, tests or docs in the working tree; git can bring it back.

EXTERNAL_SIDE_EFFECT.summary: Reaches something outside this machine that other people can see.

DESTRUCTIVE.summary: Discards work or data that git cannot bring back.

SECURITY_SENSITIVE.summary: Touches credentials, permissions or anything that grants access.

FINANCIAL.summary: Costs the owner money, now or on the next invoice.

//never_standing: An approval for a `never_standing` class authorises ONE action, matched by fingerprint, and is consumed when used. A grant to buy one thing can never authorise buying another.

rules.pattern: subscription|billing|invoice|paid plan|upgrade .*plan|purchase|\bbuy\b|pricing tier|credit card|api credits|paid (api|account|tier)|register .*domain|provision .*(cloud|instance|cluster)|\b(stripe|terraform apply|npm publish|gh release)\b
rules.reason: Anything that can appear on an invoice needs a fresh, single-use authorisation from the owner.
Cloud CLIs create billable resources; the free-looking subcommands are not distinguishable here.
ADR-0010 already bars agents from production; this keeps the same line in the collaboration layer.
Production hostnames. The dev host is dev.aweiro.com and is matched by the dev-host rule below.
Editing the deploy path is one command away from running it.
Credentials are never read, written or quoted through this layer.
Discards work or data git cannot restore.
Leaves this machine and is visible to other people; push also starts CI.
The dev backend is where agents are meant to work.
Ordinary work in the working tree.
